subject: Request: secure development controls evidence (short‑lived tokens & branch protections)
messages:
From: Eve Larson <eve.larson@acme-assessors.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood-inference.com
Cc: sam.healy@atlasbank.com
Date: 2029-12-05T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Request: secure development controls evidence (short‑lived tokens & branch protections)

Irene,

Thanks again for taking the time on our intake call earlier. As part of the SIG assessment scope for Atlas Bank we need: a concise artifact set demonstrating your controls for (1) short‑lived deploy/service tokens and rotation policy, (2) branch protection enforcement and any temporary exception logging, and (3) CI runner isolation for 3rd‑party integrations.

Can you provide the following items by EOD 2029‑12‑06?
- HashiCorp Vault policy snippets and the K/V paths you use for ephemeral tokens
- A CSV export of branch protection exceptions (with repo, approver, reason, timestamp) for the last 6 months
- CI runner inventory showing which runners are dedicated, ephemeral, or shared and any 3rd‑party marketplace actions
- Example PR approval audit trail for a critical repo (redacted) — at least 6 months

If any of these are sensitive and need secure transfer, let us know and we can provide an intake S3 link and MFT details.

Best,
Eve Larson
Senior Assessor | Acme Assessors
--
Attachment stubs: request-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood-inference.com>
To: Eve Larson <eve.larson@acme-assessors.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2029-12-05T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: secure development controls evidence (short‑lived tokens & branch protections)

Hi Eve — thanks for the clear list. We can provide all of that. A couple quick clarifications so we bundle correctly:

1) For the Vault policies: do you need the full policy files or redacted paths (we can provide both a redacted artifact and a link to a zipped bundle via secure intake)?
2) Branch protection exceptions: do you want all exceptions for all repos or only those classified as "critical"? We maintain an exceptions ledger per repo with approver and justification.
3) PR audit trail: we can export per‑repo approval logs (signed commits + approver metadata). We will redact author emails but keep approver principal names and timestamps.

Plan: Jordan will pull the branch exception export, Marissa will prepare runner/CI isolation matrix, and I will extract the Vault policy snippets and the PR audit CSV. We anticipate a single zip with the following files: vault-policies.yaml (redacted and full), ci-runner-isolation-matrix.csv, branch-protection-exceptions-202906-202912.csv, pr-approval-audit-6mo.csv.

If that works, we will drop the zip into the secure Drive folder and send you a signed access link. Expect initial package by EOD 2029‑12‑06.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
--
Attachment stubs: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Eve Larson <eve.larson@acme-assessors.com>
Date: 2029-12-05T13:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: secure development controls evidence (short‑lived tokens & branch protections)

Irene / Marissa — grabbing the branch protection exceptions now. Quick notes for the bundle:
- I filtered to repos tagged "prod" and "critical" per Atlas Bank scope; full repo set is large so we default to critical unless Eve confirms otherwise.
- CSV columns: repo_name, path, exception_id, approver, justification_summary, created_at, closed_at (if applicable).
- We found a handful of temporary bypasses for automated dependency updates (dependabot) where ops approved a narrow exception window; those are included with approval notes.

I will attach branch-protection-exceptions-202906-202912.csv to the package.

-Jordan
Engineering Security
Redwood Inference

From: Eve Larson <eve.larson@acme-assessors.com>

Date: 2029-12-06T08:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: secure development controls evidence (short‑lived tokens & branch protections)

Irene, Jordan — that scope looks good. Two requests before you bundle:
1) Please include a short README (text) that maps filenames to the control statement we are validating (so the assessor can quickly connect artifacts to SIG control IDs).
2) We still need the PR approval audit trail for the last 6 months covering at least the "infra-config" and "runtime" repos — redactions OK but keep approver identities and timestamps.

If you can't make EOD, a partial drop with Vault policies + runner matrix would be helpful this morning.

Thanks — Eve
--
Attachment stubs: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Eve Larson <eve.larson@acme-assessors.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>, Sam Healy <sam.healy@atlasbank.com>
Date: 2029-12-06T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: secure development controls evidence (short‑lived tokens & branch protections)

Eve — attaching the package we discussed. Delivery notes below and a short README inside the zip that maps artifacts to SIG controls.

Delivered artifacts (zip):
- vault-policies.yaml (includes example ephemeral token policy and references to K/V paths: secret/ephemeral/deploy/*)
- ci-runner-isolation-matrix.csv (runner_id, runner_type, dedicated_to, image_whitelist, last_patch_date)
- branch-protection-exceptions-202906-202912.csv (filtered to repos: infra-config, runtime, auth-service, billing)
- pr-approval-audit-6mo.csv (repo, pr_id, approver, approval_timestamp, commit_signoff, redaction_flag)
- README-map.txt (artifact -> SIG control mapping; contact for intake)

Notes:
- PR audit contains approver names and timestamps; author emails and commit hashes are redacted in the delivered CSV but full signed commit SHAs can be provided under an NDA if needed.
- Runner isolation matrix highlights three ephemeral runner pools used for third‑party marketplace actions; those pools run in dedicated VPC subnets and are rotated nightly.
- Vault policy snippet shows TTL defaults (3600s) for short‑lived tokens and our rotation job that revokes stale tokens daily.

If you need a signed S3 transfer or a PGP bundle instead of Drive, tell us and we will reupload.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Security Operations
Redwood Inference
--
Attachment stubs: vault-policies.yaml (text/yaml), ci-runner-isolation-matrix.csv (text/csv), branch-protection-exceptions-202906-202912.csv (text/csv), pr-approval-audit-6mo.csv (text/csv), README-map.txt (text/plain)
